info.title: Fel's Voice Lab HTTP API
info.summary: The local service behind the Voice Lab's pages, for scripts and other programs.
info.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. JSON in, JSON out, except where a call returns audio. Every error is a JSON object with an `error` message. See docs/API.md for the conventions, the speaking calls and the command-line tool.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Is it running, what is loaded, which engines exist. None of these makes audio, except an engine check.

tags.name: Speaking
tags.description: Turn text into audio. `speak` and `performance` answer with the finished WAV file in one response.

tags.name: OpenAI-style
tags.description: For apps that can send text to any server that answers like OpenAI's speech API: give them `http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1` as the base address and any key. The Lab's voices, by the names `GET /api/voices` gives; nothing is kept in the library. Errors take OpenAI's shape: `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`, with the Lab's `code`.

tags.name: Cast
tags.description: Characters, the voices (identities) they speak with, the recordings that clone those voices, and pronunciations. Retiring blocks new use of an item and everything made from it; purging deletes it.

tags.name: Takes
tags.description: Saved performances. Every `performance` call and every scene render saves a take with its text, settings, model and provenance. An edit of a take (a trim, a cut of the silence, fades, a gain) is saved as a new take that names its original.

tags.name: Scenes
tags.description: Ordered scripts rendered line by line through the same performance call. The manifest's fields are in [scene-schema-v1.md](scenes/scene-schema-v1.md).

tags.name: Live speech
tags.description: Short-lived sessions with ordered local audio input and speech replies.

tags.name: Automation
tags.description: Saved local recipes, provider profiles and resumable runs.

tags.name: Production
tags.description: Search saved projects and share local project or voice files.

tags.name: Books
tags.description: Local manuscript import, editable chapter scenes, chapter auditions and audiobook packages.

tags.name: Exports
tags.description: Delivery packages: a scene's selected takes, converted, checked and written to `out/exports`.

tags.name: Comparisons
tags.description: Listening comparisons and blind A/B sessions. See [evaluation-schema-v1.md](evaluation/evaluation-schema-v1.md).

tags.name: Conversion
tags.description: Voice conversion: say a recording again in another voice.

tags.name: System
tags.description: The service's report, folder sizes, library backups and housekeeping.

get.summary: Say whether the service is ready, and which version it is.

200.description: `status` (`ready`, or `busy` while a model loads or generates), `busy`, `device`, `version`, `workers` (one entry per loaded engine), `last_worker_error`, `last_unload`, `app` (`Fel's Voice Lab`, so a program can tell the Lab from something else on the port), `lab_id` (the same for every service of one Lab folder and library) and `fels` (`contract`, `app` (`voice-lab`), `version` and `api`: how the other apps of Fel's Studio recognise the Lab, fels_suite.py).

get.summary: Name the device, the loaded engines, the Kokoro and Phonon voices found and the free memory.

200.description: `device`, `loaded` (the engines in memory), `voices` (Kokoro voice names), `kokoro_languages`, `phonon_voices` (the installed Phonon voices, each with `name`, `group`, `character`, `gender`, `age`, `locale` and `description`) and `free_ram_gb`.

get.summary: List every engine the Lab knows, with its support level, pinned checkpoint, capabilities and license.

200.description: The engine catalog. An engine's `id` is the `engine` of the speaking calls; only engines whose `integration.service_api` is true answer them. `support` is `supported` (tested for every release on the Lab's test GPU and on the CPU where it runs), `works` (tested when it changes) or `experimental` (may break or have limits, described in `support_note`). Each engine has a `licence` rating and reason, and can have a separate `preset_licence` for its voice catalog. Each engine also has `facts`, what its card on the Models page says, from the catalog, its adapter, its installer and the language screen: `first_model` (marked as a good first model), and `runs` (`cpu`, `gpu`, `gpu_memory_gb`), `voices` (`clones`, `presets`, `designs`, `converts`), `direction` (`takes`, `acts_tags`), `languages` (`offered`, each `label`, `language` and its `screen` result; `filter`, the languages the page's question matches) and `output` (`status`), each with its `text` in plain words.

get.summary: Say which engines are installed and usable here, and what each check measured. Reads files and stored results only.

200.description: `device` (the service's: `cuda` for a graphics card, or `cpu`), `busy`, `engines` (one row per catalog engine: `id`, `name`, `integrated`, `installation`, `state`, `check`, `check_outdated`, `min_free_ram_gb`, `device` and, for an integrated engine, `switch`, `device_choice` and `gpu`), `ram`, `install`, `speed` and `store_error`. `installation` holds `installed`, `missing` (the files not found), `environment`, `checkpoint` and, while files are missing from an engine that has a guided installer, `installer`: the launcher in the lab folder that installs it. `min_free_ram_gb` is the free RAM in GB the Lab wants before it loads the engine (`null` when none is set), and `ram` is this computer's `total_gb` and `free_gb`. An engine's `device` is the one its worker is asked for, and `check` is its last check there. `switch` is what its GPU/CPU switch shows (`gpu` or `cpu`), `device_choice` the choice kept for it (`null` when it follows the service), and `gpu` holds `choosable` (GPU can be picked), `reason` (why not), `build` (the PyTorch build in its environment: `cuda`, `rocm`, `cpu` or `null`) and `install` (Install puts in its GPU build). An engine that is not installed and has a guided installer also has `install_size`: `download_bytes` and `disk_bytes` for a first install of the build its Install puts in, from the installer's own numbers (its plan gives the exact figure), or `null` when they cannot be read. `install` is the latest install started from the Models page, or `null` when none has run since the service started: `id`, `engine`, `name`, `nvidia` (requests a GPU build), `state` (`running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `finished` or `failed`), `phase` (`preparing`, `environment`, `packages`, `downloading`, `unpacking`, `checking`, `finishing`, `waiting` or `null`), `started_at`, `ended_at`, `seconds`, `exit_code`, `lines` (the end of its output) and `log` (all of it, a path under the lab folder). A card that can retry an interrupted install has `install_resume` with its `nvidia` choice and the `phase` where it was interrupted.

post.summary: Check that one engine can speak now: confirm its files, load it and speak one short clip.

wait_seconds.description: Wait in line up to this many seconds (at most 3600) while the model worker is busy, instead of the 409 answered at once without it. See `GET /api/queue`.

wait_priority.description: `normal` (the default), or `low` to wait behind the others, as a scene batch's lines do.

parameters.name: engine_id
parameters.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog`.

200.description: `check`: `status` (`passed`, `failed` or `not_installed`), `device`, `ran_on`, `checked_at`, `reason`, `load_seconds`, `total_s`, `audio_seconds`, `real_time_factor` and, for a missing install, `missing`. Takes seconds to minutes; the result is kept and shows in `GET /api/engines/status`.

400.description: The engine is unknown, or is not a speech engine.

409.description: The model worker is busy and the request sent no `wait_seconds`, waited that long, or found 20 requests already waiting. Or, with `code` `gpu_busy`, the model would load on the graphics card while another app of Fel's Studio has it to itself (NPC Forge's One model at a time): refused at once, even with `wait_seconds`, and `holder` names that app, what it is doing and since when.

499.description: The request was cancelled with `POST /api/queue/{request_id}/cancel`: while it waited, or while it ran.

post.summary: Install an engine with its guided installer (every engine in the catalog has one): read its plan, or run the installer.

dry_run.description: Only read the plan: what the installer would do and whether this computer can take it. Nothing is changed. Default false, which starts the install.

nvidia.description: Install the engine's GPU build for this computer's graphics card (its installer's `--gpu`): NVIDIA's CUDA build, or AMD's ROCm build on a computer whose card is an AMD Radeon. An engine installed with the CPU build of PyTorch can get it afterwards. The Qwen3-TTS models, VoxCPM2 and Breeze TTS 2 run only on a graphics card and always get the GPU build, whatever this says. Default false.

parameters.name: engine_id
parameters.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog`.

200.description: With `dry_run`, `plan`: `engine`, `nvidia`, `ok`, `paragraphs` (the plan, one string for each paragraph or numbered step) and `problems` (why it cannot go ahead; empty when `ok`). Otherwise `install`: the job that started, as in `GET /api/engines/status`, which is the route to poll for its progress. The job runs the script the engine's launcher runs, with `--yes`. While it runs the service refuses every other load, check and clip.

400.description: The engine is unknown, has no installer (or no GPU build) in the app, or is installed already; or `dry_run` or `nvidia` is not true or false.

409.description: An install is already running, or the model worker is busy.

post.summary: Stop a guided model install. An active package command finishes first. Resumable model downloads are kept.

parameters.name: engine_id
parameters.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog`.

200.description: `install`: the matching job, as in `GET /api/engines/status`. Poll until its state is final.

400.description: The job id is missing or invalid.

409.description: The current install does not match this job.

post.summary: Uninstall a model: read what it would delete, or delete its files from the Lab's folder.
post.description: A model's files are its checkpoint in `hf-cache`, with its preset voices' repository; the files it keeps elsewhere (Breeze in `breeze/models`, Drama 3 in `out/drama3`); its worker's source folders (VoxCPM2 in `out/voxcpm2`); and its own Python environment (`.venv-kokoro`). What another installed model uses stays: the Chatterbox models share a checkpoint and `.venv-chatterbox`, the Qwen3-TTS models `.venv-fqwen`, which VoxCPM2 also borrows from. The service's own `.venv` and the library are never touched. Every model is unloaded first, and the model worker refuses other work until the files are gone. Install on the model's card puts it back.

dry_run.description: Only read the plan: what would be deleted and what stays. Nothing is changed. Default false, which deletes.

parameters.name: engine_id
parameters.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog`.

200.description: With `dry_run`, `plan`: `engine`, `name`, `remove` (each folder's `path` in the Lab's folder, its `bytes`, and `link` when it is a link or junction, which is removed as a link and never followed), `keep` (each folder that stays, with `why`), `bytes`, `ok`, `paragraphs` and `problems`. Otherwise `uninstall`: the plan with `removed`, `failed` (each `path` with its `reason`, such as a file another program has open) and `freed` bytes.

400.description: The engine is unknown, or has no files of its own to delete (another installed model uses them all), or `dry_run` is not true or false.

409.description: An install is running, or the model worker is busy.

post.description: The other apps of Fel's Studio call this before NPC Forge takes the graphics card to itself (its One model at a time switch). Without `wait_seconds` a busy Lab answers 409 at once; with it, the request waits its turn in line, but a scene being spoken is refused at once, since it would wait for the whole scene. After the unload the Lab no longer holds the GPU lock of Fel's Studio (`GET /api/gpu`). docs/CONNECT.md says more.

200.description: `device` (this service's, `cuda` or `cpu`), `held` (whether a model of this service is on the graphics card now), `holders` (each app holding the lock, oldest first: `app`, `name`, `pid`, `what` (the model or the work), `since`, `alone` and `this_service`) and `alone` (the app that has the card to itself or is clearing it for itself, with the same fields, or null). get.summary: Describe the settings each engine's performance takes, and the languages its picker offers.

200.description: `engines`: for each engine its controls (name, type, range, default), whether it takes a direction, and its `languages`; and `unscreened_languages`: per engine, the languages the language screen did not clear.

get.summary: Say what the model worker is doing, and what waits for it, in order.
get.description: The worker does one load, clip, take, test or install at a time. A request that needs it while it is busy is refused with 409 at once, unless it sent `wait_seconds` in its JSON body: then it waits in line, at most that many seconds (up to 3600). Requests with `wait_priority` `low`, as a scene batch's lines send, wait behind the others, and each priority keeps its order. At most 20 wait. A waiting request leaves the line when it is cancelled, when its caller closes the connection, or when its time is up (409).

200.description: `running`: null, or the request using the worker; `waiting`: the requests in line, first first; and `max_waiting`. Each request has `id` (its `X-Request-Id`), `what` (such as `Take`, `Clip`, `Model test` or `Install`), `engine` (null when it is not one model's work), `priority` (`normal`, or `low` for a scene batch), `since` (when it started running, or joined the line), `seconds` (how long ago), `can_stop` and, for an install, `detail` (what it is installing).

post.summary: Take a request out of the line, or stop it while it runs.
post.description: Send your own `X-Request-Id` with the request you may want to stop, so you know its id before it answers.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: A request's id: the `X-Request-Id` it sent, or the one its answer names; an entry of `GET /api/queue`.

200.description: `cancelled`: `waiting` (it left the line, and answers 499 at once) or `running` (its model's process was ended: it answers 499 within moments, and the next request loads the model again).

400.description: The running request cannot be stopped: an install, or an unload.

404.description: No request with that id is waiting or running.

get.summary: Return this API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document.

200.description: The same document as `openapi.json` in the program folder, built from the route table.

get.summary: List every voice a program can speak with by name.
get.description: A Cast voice is named after its character when it is the character's only voice, or its only approved one; any Cast voice is also `Character (Label)`. Retired and rejected voices are left out. A preset voice keeps its model's name (`af_heart`, `Harper`), or is `model:voice` when a Cast voice or another model has that name. Kokoro's and Phonon's voices are those installed; a Qwen CustomVoice checkpoint's speakers are listed while it is loaded, since only the loaded checkpoint reports them. Nothing is loaded to answer.

200.description: `voices`: the Cast's voices first, then the preset voices of the models this service runs. Each has `name`, the one name to send back as `voice`; `aliases`, other names that mean it; `kind`, `cast` or `preset`; `model` and `model_name`; `label`; `languages`; `takes_direction`, whether its model uses an acting `direction`; `ready`, and `why_not`, a sentence saying what to do when it is not ready. `licence` has a `rating` (`yes`, `conditions`, `unclear` or `no`) and a `reason` for it. A Cast voice also has `character`, `identity_id` and `status`; a preset voice has `voice_id`, its model's own name for it.

post.summary: Speak text with one engine and answer with the finished WAV file.
post.description: Send no query string: `/api/speak?x=1` is a 404. Qwen, VoxCPM2 and Drama 3 refuse a field they do not take and name it in the 400. To keep what you generate as a Cast take, use [`POST /api/performance`](#post-api-performance).

text.description: What to say, 1 to 10,000 characters. Text over 1,200 characters is split where a scene splits a long line, spoken part by part in the same call and joined with a quarter-second pause; the answer is still one WAV, and `X-Parts` says how many parts it had. The call can be cancelled between parts. A voice invented from a description (design mode) is refused for such a text, since it would change from one part to the next.

engine.description: An engine id from `GET /api/catalog` whose `integration.service_api` is true. Default `kokoro`.

voice.description: Without `engine`: a voice's `name` from `GET /api/voices`. A Cast voice speaks as that voice and nothing is kept (as `POST /api/performance` with `keep_take` false: `language`, `direction`, `settings` and `use_pronunciations` go with it); a preset voice speaks with its model. With `engine` `kokoro`, or no engine: a Kokoro voice id, or several joined with commas to blend them. Default `af_heart`. Phonon: one voice name from `phonon_voices` of `GET /api/info`. Default `Harper`.

language.description: Kokoro and Qwen: the language. Default `English`, or for a Kokoro voice named without `engine`, the voice's own language. Phonon speaks English only.

voice_description.description: Qwen VoiceDesign, VoxCPM2 and Breeze design mode: the voice to invent, in words.

mode.description: For engines with several modes: `design`, `clone`, `continuation`, `custom_voice` or, for Breeze, `direction`. A checkpoint accepts the modes it supports.

reference_path.description: Cloning: a recording inside the Lab's reference storage.

reference_text.description: Cloning: the exact transcript of that recording.

direction.description: Engines with a direction control: how to deliver the line, up to 1000 characters.

seed.description: Engines that take one: the random seed. Default 42.

temperature.description: Phonon: how much the delivery varies, 0 to 1. Default 0.3. The other engines that take a temperature list theirs under `capabilities` in `GET /api/catalog`.

duration_delta.description: Phonon: shift the pace, from -0.5 (faster) to 0.5 (slower). Default 0.

save_voice_as.description: Design mode only: keep the invented voice as a reusable reference under this name, letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to two folders deep.

wait_seconds.description: Wait in line up to this many seconds (at most 3600) while the model worker is busy, instead of the 409 answered at once without it. See `GET /api/queue`.

wait_priority.description: `normal` (the default), or `low` to wait behind the others, as a scene batch's lines do.

200.description: The whole 16-bit WAV file, in one response with a `Content-Length`. The call blocks until the clip is finished; there is no streaming and no partial answer. Other engine-specific fields are listed under each engine's `capabilities` in `GET /api/catalog`.

X-Audio-Seconds.description: Seconds of audio in the file.

X-First-Chunk.description: Seconds to the first audio, when the engine reports it; otherwise empty.

X-Generation-Mode.description: The mode the engine ran in, when it reports one.

X-Checkpoint-Revision.description: The checkpoint's pinned revision, when reported.

X-Voice-Asset-Path.description: With `save_voice_as`: the file the voice was saved to.

X-Parts.description: How many parts a text over 1,200 characters was spoken in.

404.description: `voice` names no voice in `GET /api/voices` and is not a Kokoro voice id.

500.description: The model is installed but could not load or run; `error` says what it reported.

503.description: The model is not installed (`code` `model_not_installed`). `error` begins by saying where to install it: Install on its Models & features card, or its launcher in the lab folder with the arguments that choose the model: `tools\setup-kokoro.bat`, `tools\setup-phonon.bat`, `tools\setup-chatterbox.bat` (Chatterbox Turbo, or with `--original` Chatterbox 500M and Voice Conversion), `tools\setup-qwen.bat` with `--model` and the Qwen3-TTS model, `tools\setup-voxcpm.bat`, `tools\setup-breeze.bat` or `tools\setup-drama3.bat`.

504.description: The engine did not answer in time.

409.description: `save_voice_as` names a voice that already exists (`code` `already_exists`); or the model worker is busy and the request sent no `wait_seconds`, waited that long, or found 20 requests already waiting. Or, with `code` `gpu_busy`, the model would load on the graphics card while another app of Fel's Studio has it to itself (NPC Forge's One model at a time): refused at once, even with `wait_seconds`, and `holder` names that app, what it is doing and since when.

499.description: The request was cancelled with `POST /api/queue/{request_id}/cancel`: while it waited, or while it ran.

A failure after the first line arrives as an `error` line, not a status code.

post.summary: Speak a line as a Cast voice, and save it as a take unless asked not to.
post.description: See [Speak as a Cast voice](#speak-as-a-cast-voice) for how to find the ids and what a retry does.

identity_id.description: The voice identity to speak with, from `GET /api/cast`. Give this or `voice`.

voice.description: A Cast voice's `name` from `GET /api/voices`, instead of `identity_id`.

text.description: The line, 1 to 1200 characters; with `keep_take` false, up to 10,000. Text over 1,200 characters is split where a scene splits a long line, spoken part by part in the same call and joined with a quarter-second pause; the answer is still one WAV, and `X-Parts` says how many parts it had. The call can be cancelled between parts. A voice invented from a description (design mode) is refused for such a text, since it would change from one part to the next.

keep_take.description: Default true: the clip is saved as a take. False saves nothing in the library, for a program that speaks all day; the clip is still labelled as AI-generated speech.

line_id.description: Your own label for the line, 1 to 100 characters. Takes are grouped by voice and line. Needed when the take is kept.

reference_version_id.description: The recording to clone from. Default: the identity's approved recording. Refused for a fixed or preset voice.

The steps run in this order: trim to `start_seconds` to `end_seconds`; auto-trim inside that range (quiet inside the speech is never cut); the two fades, on a raised-cosine curve; then the gain. A trim alone copies the samples exactly; a fade or a gain recalculates them and rounds back to 16 bits. The new take keeps the parent's text, voice, settings and model, starts as a `candidate`, and has its loudness and checks measured again. Its word and phoneme times, when the parent has them, move with the trim, and a word the trim cuts away leaves them. An edit of an edit is allowed. Retiring a take retires its edits, and purging it deletes them.
